sanskrit: vadhābhiprāyam āyāntam avadhīs tvaṃ mahābalam rakṣasas tasya bhaginī kiṃ naḥ kruddhā kariṣyati
english: You slew that mighty demon who came with murderous intent — what then can his sister do to us, even if she is enraged?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hiḍimbā tu tataḥ kuntīm abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca kaunteyam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hiḍimbā then bowed before Kuntī with joined palms and spoke these words to Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: ārye jānāsi yad duḥkham iha strīṇām anaṅgajam tad idaṃ mām anuprāptaṃ bhīmasenakṛtaṃ śubhe
english: "O noble lady, you know what suffering arises in women from the god of love — that very affliction, caused by Bhīmasena, has now come upon me, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: soḍhaṃ tat paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ mayā kālapratīkṣayā so 'yam abhyāgataḥ kālo bhavitā me sukhāya vai
english: I have endured that supreme anguish while biding my time — and now that moment has arrived, which shall bring me happiness at last.

sanskrit: mayā hy utsṛjya suhṛdaḥ svadharmaṃ svajanaṃ tathā vṛto 'yaṃ puruṣavyāghras tava putraḥ patiḥ śubhe
english: For I abandoned my friends, my own dharma, and my own people, and chose this tiger among men, your son, as my husband, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: vareṇāpi tathānena tvayā cāpi yaśasvini tathā bruvantī hi tadā pratyākhyātā kriyāṃ prati
english: Yet even though I spoke in this way, I was rejected by this man — and by you too, O illustrious one — regarding the act I sought.

sanskrit: tvaṃ māṃ mūḍheti vā matvā bhaktā vānugateti vā bhartrānena mahābhāge saṃyojaya sutena te
english: Whether you consider me foolish or devoted and submissive, O greatly fortunate one, please unite me with your son as my husband.

sanskrit: tam upādāya gaccheyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ devarūpiṇam punaś caivāgamiṣyāmi viśrambhaṃ kuru me śubhe
english: Taking him — who is beautiful as a god — I shall go wherever I wish, and I shall return again; place your trust in me, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi manasā dhyātā sarvān neṣyāmi vaḥ sadā vṛjine tārayiṣyāmi durgeṣu ca nararṣabhān
english: For when summoned in thought, I shall always carry all of you away; I shall deliver these bull-like men from danger and through difficult passages.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhena vo vahiṣyāmi śīghrāṃ gatim abhīpsataḥ yūyaṃ prasādaṃ kuruta bhīmaseno bhajeta mām
english: I shall carry you all on my back, as swift as you could desire — grant me your grace, and let Bhīmasena take me as his wife."

sanskrit: āpadas taraṇe prāṇān dhārayed yena yena hi sarvam ādṛtya kartavyaṃ tad dharmam anuvartatā
english: By whatever means one may sustain one's life in crossing calamities, all of that must be done with care — for it is dharma that guides such action.

sanskrit: āpatsu yo dhārayati dharmaṃ dharmavid uttamaḥ vyasanaṃ hy eva dharmasya dharmiṇām āpad ucyate
english: The highest knower of dharma is one who upholds dharma even in misfortune — for indeed, calamity itself is said to be the test of dharma for the righteous.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ prāṇān dhārayati puṇyaṃ prāṇadam ucyate yena yenācared dharmaṃ tasmin garhā na vidyate
english: Virtue sustains life; virtue is what is called life-giving — whatever means one employs to practise dharma, no blame attaches to that.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca evam etad yathāttha tvaṃ hiḍimbe nātra saṃśayaḥ sthātavyaṃ tu tvayā dharme yathā brūyāṃ sumadhyame
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "It is exactly as you have said, Hiḍimbā — there is no doubt in this. But you must abide by dharma as I shall prescribe, O slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: snātaṃ kṛtāhnikaṃ bhadre kṛtakautukamaṅgalam bhīmasenaṃ bhajethās tvaṃ prāg astagamanād raveḥ
english: Having bathed and completed the daily rites, and with auspicious ornaments put on, you may enjoy Bhīmasena's company, O blessed one, before the sun sets.

sanskrit: ahaḥsu viharānena yathākāmaṃ manojavā ayaṃ tv ānayitavyas te bhīmasenaḥ sadā niśi
english: During the daytime roam with him as you wish, O swift as thought — but Bhīmasena must be brought back to us every night."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatheti tat pratijñāya hiḍimbā rākṣasī tadā bhīmasenam upādāya ūrdhvam ācakrame tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Agreeing to this with the words "so be it," the rakshasi Hiḍimbā thereupon took Bhīmasena and soared up into the sky.

sanskrit: śailaśṛṅgeṣu ramyeṣu devatāyataneṣu ca mṛgapakṣivighuṣṭeṣu ramaṇīyeṣu sarvadā
english: On the lovely peaks of mountains, in the sanctuaries of the gods, in places always charming and resounding with the cries of deer and birds —

sanskrit: kṛtvā ca paramaṃ rūpaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā saṃjalpantī sumadhuraṃ ramayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: — assuming her most beautiful form, adorned with all ornaments, conversing with sweetest words, she delighted the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tathaiva vanadurgeṣu puṣpitadrumasānuṣu saraḥsu ramaṇīyeṣu padmotpalayuteṣu ca
english: Likewise on the steep slopes of forests adorned with flowering trees, at lovely lakes covered with lotuses and water-lilies,

sanskrit: nadīdvīpapradeśeṣu vaiḍūryasikatāsu ca sutīrthavanatoyāsu tathā girinadīṣu ca
english: on river islands and shore-lands, on sands gleaming like beryl, at forest streams with good fords, and at mountain rivers,

sanskrit: sagarasya pradeśeṣu maṇihemaciteṣu ca pattaneṣu ca ramyeṣu mahāśālavaneṣu ca
english: on shores of the ocean strewn with gems and gold, in beautiful harbor-towns, and in great forests of śāla trees,

sanskrit: devāraṇyeṣu puṇyeṣu tathā parvatasānuṣu guhyakānāṃ nivāseṣu tāpasāyataneṣu ca
english: in sacred groves of the gods and on mountain plateaus, in the abodes of the Guhyakas and in the hermitages of ascetics,

sanskrit: sarvartuphalapuṣpeṣu mānaseṣu saraḥsu ca bibhratī paramaṃ rūpaṃ ramayām āsa pāṇḍavam
english: at the Mānasa lakes bearing fruits and flowers of every season — bearing her most beautiful form, she delighted the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: ramayantī tathā bhīmaṃ tatra tatra manojavā prajajñe rākṣasī putraṃ bhīmasenān mahābalam
english: As she thus sported with Bhīma here and there, swift as thought, the rakshasi conceived and bore from Bhīmasena a mighty son.

sanskrit: virūpākṣaṃ mahāvaktraṃ śaṅkukarṇaṃ vibhīṣaṇam bhīmarūpaṃ sutāmroṣṭhaṃ tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭraṃ mahābalam
english: He had misshapen eyes and a huge mouth; his ears were spike-like; he was terrifying to behold; his form was fearsome; his lips were copper-red; his teeth were sharp; and he was immensely powerful.

sanskrit: maheṣvāsaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahāsattvaṃ mahābhujam mahājavaṃ mahākāyaṃ mahāmāyam ariṃdamam
english: He was a mighty archer, of great valor, great strength, mighty-armed, of great speed, of great body, possessed of great illusions, and a subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: amānuṣaṃ mānuṣajaṃ bhīmavegaṃ mahābalam yaḥ piśācān atīvānyān babhūvāti sa mānuṣān
english: Non-human yet born of a human, of terrible speed and great power — he surpassed other piśācas exceedingly, just as he surpassed ordinary humans.

sanskrit: bālo 'pi yauvanaṃ prāpto mānuṣeṣu viśāṃ pate sarvāstreṣu paraṃ vīraḥ prakarṣam agamad balī
english: Even as a child he attained youth — O lord of the people — and that mighty hero achieved supreme excellence in all weapons.

sanskrit: sadyo hi garbhaṃ rākṣasyo labhante prasavanti ca kāmarūpadharāś caiva bhavanti bahurūpiṇaḥ
english: For rakshasa women conceive and give birth at once; they can assume any form at will and take on many shapes.

sanskrit: praṇamya vikacaḥ pādāv agṛhṇāt sa pitus tadā mātuś ca parameṣvāsas tau ca nāmāsya cakratuḥ
english: Bowing in reverence, Vikaca — that greatest of archers — clasped the feet of both his father and his mother, and they gave him his name.

sanskrit: ghaṭabhāsotkaca iti mātaraṃ so 'bhyabhāṣata abhavat tena nāmāsya ghaṭotkaca iti sma ha
english: He addressed his mother as "Ghaṭabhāsotkaca," and from that name his own name became Ghaṭotkaca — so it is told.

sanskrit: anuraktaś ca tān āsīt pāṇḍavān sa ghaṭotkacaḥ teṣāṃ ca dayito nityam ātmabhūto babhūva saḥ
english: Ghaṭotkaca was devoted to the Pāṇḍavas, and he became always dear to them, as if he were one of themselves.

sanskrit: saṃvāsasamayo jīrṇa ity abhāṣata taṃ tataḥ hiḍimbā samayaṃ kṛtvā svāṃ gatiṃ pratyapadyata
english: Then Hiḍimbā spoke to him saying "the time of our living together is spent" — and having made her covenant, she returned to her own way.

sanskrit: kṛtyakāla upasthāsye pitṝn iti ghaṭotkacaḥ āmantrya rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ pratasthe cottarāṃ diśam
english: "I shall come to you, O fathers, when the time of need arrives" — saying this, Ghaṭotkaca, foremost of rakshasas, took leave and departed toward the northern direction.

sanskrit: sa hi sṛṣṭo maghavatā śaktihetor mahātmanā karṇasyāprativīryasya vināśāya mahātmanaḥ
english: For he had been created by the great Indra, the lord of treasures, for the sake of the śakti weapon — to be the instrument of death for the irresistibly mighty Karṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te vanena vanaṃ vīrā ghnanto mṛgagaṇān bahūn apakramya yayū rājaṃs tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those heroes, those great warriors, hastening onward, passed from forest to forest, slaying many herds of deer as they went, O king.

sanskrit: matsyāṃs trigartān pāñcālān kīcakān antareṇa ca ramaṇīyān vanoddeśān prekṣamāṇāḥ sarāṃsi ca
english: Passing through the lands of the Matsyas, Trigartas, Pāñcālas, and Kīcakas, they looked upon lovely forest regions and lakes.

sanskrit: jaṭāḥ kṛtvātmanaḥ sarve valkalājinavāsasaḥ saha kuntyā mahātmāno bibhratas tāpasaṃ vapuḥ
english: All of them, those great souls, had matted their hair; they were clad in bark garments and deer-skins; along with Kuntī they bore the appearance of ascetics.

sanskrit: kva cid vahanto jananīṃ tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ kva cic chandena gacchantas te jagmuḥ prasabhaṃ punaḥ
english: Sometimes those great warriors carried their mother in haste; sometimes they moved at their own pace — and so they journeyed on repeatedly.

sanskrit: brāhmaṃ vedam adhīyānā vedāṅgāni ca sarvaśaḥ nītiśāstraṃ ca dharmajñā dadṛśus te pitāmaham
english: Studying the Vedas of Brahmā, all the Vedic auxiliaries, and the science of statecraft, those knowers of dharma beheld their grandfather.

sanskrit: te 'bhivādya mahātmānaṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaṃ tadā tasthuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve saha mātrā paraṃtapāḥ
english: They bowed in reverence to that great soul, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, and then all of them, scorchers of foes, stood with joined palms, together with their mother.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca mayedaṃ manasā pūrvaṃ viditaṃ bharatarṣabhāḥ yathā sthitair adharmeṇa dhārtarāṣṭrair vivāsitāḥ
english: Vyāsa said: "O bulls of the Bhārata line, I had known this beforehand in my mind — how you were exiled through the unrighteous conduct of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tad viditvāsmi saṃprāptaś cikīrṣuḥ paramaṃ hitam na viṣādo 'tra kartavyaḥ sarvam etat sukhāya vaḥ
english: Knowing that, I have come, wishing to do what is supremely good for you. No despondency should be felt here — all of this will lead to your happiness.

sanskrit: samās te caiva me sarve yūyaṃ caiva na saṃśayaḥ dīnato bālataś caiva snehaṃ kurvanti bāndhavāḥ
english: They are all equal to me, and you as well — there is no doubt of this. Kinsmen form attachments from helplessness and from childhood alike.

sanskrit: tasmād abhyadhikaḥ sneho yuṣmāsu mama sāṃpratam snehapūrvaṃ cikīrṣāmi hitaṃ vas tan nibodhata
english: Therefore my affection for you is especially great at this time. I wish to do what is beneficial for you, out of that love — hear this from me.

sanskrit: idaṃ nagaram abhyāśe ramaṇīyaṃ nirāmayam vasateha praticchannā mamāgamanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Near here is a beautiful and wholesome city — dwell there in concealment, awaiting my return."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sa tān samāśvāsya vyāsaḥ pārthān ariṃdamān ekacakrām abhigataḥ kuntīm āśvāsayat prabhuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus comforted those sons of Pṛthā, the tamers of foes, the lord Vyāsa went to Ekacakrā and comforted Kuntī.

sanskrit: jīvaputri sutas te 'yaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ pṛthivyāṃ pārthivān sarvān praśāsiṣyati dharmarāṭ
english: "Long live your sons, O daughter — this son of yours, Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, shall rule as king of dharma over all the kings of the earth.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa jitvā pṛthivīm akhilāṃ dharmavid vaśī bhīmasenārjunabalād bhokṣyaty ayam asaṃśayaḥ
english: Knowing dharma, self-controlled, he shall conquer the entire earth by dharma and enjoy it with the strength of Bhīmasena and Arjuna — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: putrās tava ca mādryāś ca sarva eva mahārathāḥ svarāṣṭre vihariṣyanti sukhaṃ sumanasas tadā
english: Both your sons and the sons of Mādrī — all of them great warriors — shall then sport happily and with joyful minds in their own kingdom.

sanskrit: yakṣyanti ca naravyāghrā vijitya pṛthivīm imām rājasūyāśvamedhādyaiḥ kratubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: These tigers among men shall, having conquered this earth, perform great sacrifices — the Rājasūya, the Aśvamedha, and others — with abundant sacrificial fees.

sanskrit: anugṛhya suhṛdvargaṃ dhanena ca sukhena ca pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyam iha bhokṣyanti te sutāḥ
english: Bestowing favour upon their circle of friends with wealth and happiness, your sons shall here enjoy the kingdom of their fathers and grandfathers."

sanskrit: evam uktvā niveśyainān brāhmaṇasya niveśane abravīt pārthivaśreṣṭham ṛṣir dvaipāyanas tadā
english: Having spoken thus and settled them in the dwelling of a brahmin, the sage Dvaipāyana then spoke to the best of princes, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: iha māṃ saṃpratīkṣadhvam āgamiṣyāmy ahaṃ punaḥ deśakālau viditvaiva vetsyadhvaṃ paramāṃ mudam
english: "Await me here — I shall come again. Knowing the right place and time, you shall attain the highest joy."

sanskrit: sa taiḥ prāñjalibhiḥ sarvais tathety ukto narādhipa jagāma bhagavān vyāso yathākāmam ṛṣiḥ prabhuḥ
english: Answered with "so be it" by all of them with joined palms, O lord of men, the blessed sage Vyāsa, the lord, departed as he wished.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca ekacakrāṃ gatās te tu kuntīputrā mahārathāḥ ataḥ paraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha kim akurvata pāṇḍavāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: "After those mighty warriors, the sons of Kuntī, had gone to Ekacakrā, what did the Pāṇḍavas do next, O best of the twice-born?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ekacakrāṃ gatās te tu kuntīputrā mahārathāḥ ūṣur nāticiraṃ kālaṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those mighty warriors, the sons of Kuntī, having gone to Ekacakrā, dwelt for no very long time in the dwelling of a brahmin.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyāni paśyanto vanāni vividhāni ca pārthivān api coddeśān saritaś ca sarāṃsi ca
english: They beheld the charming forests, various and beautiful, and royal districts too, and rivers and lakes.

sanskrit: cerur bhaikṣaṃ tadā te tu sarva eva viśāṃ pate babhūvur nāgarāṇāṃ ca svair guṇaiḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: They wandered begging for alms, all of them, O lord of the people, and by their own virtues became dear to the eyes of the townspeople.

sanskrit: nivedayanti sma ca te bhaikṣaṃ kuntyāḥ sadā niśi tayā vibhaktān bhāgāṃs te bhuñjate sma pṛthak pṛthak
english: Every evening they would present the alms they had gathered to Kuntī; and they would eat the portions she distributed, each separately.

sanskrit: ardhaṃ te bhuñjate vīrāḥ saha mātrā paraṃtapāḥ ardhaṃ bhaikṣasya sarvasya bhīmo bhuṅkte mahābalaḥ
english: Half of the food those heroes, those scorchers of foes, ate together with their mother; the other half of all the alms the mighty Bhīma ate alone.

sanskrit: tathā tu teṣāṃ vasatāṃ tatra rājan mahātmanām aticakrāma sumahān kālo 'tha bharatarṣabha
english: Now while those great souls were dwelling there, O king, a very long time passed, O bull of the Bhārata line.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid bhaikṣāya gatās te bharatarṣabhāḥ saṃgatyā bhīmasenas tu tatrāste pṛthayā saha
english: Then one day those bulls of the Bhārata line had gone out to beg for alms, and by chance Bhīmasena remained there with Pṛthā.

sanskrit: athārtijaṃ mahāśabdaṃ brāhmaṇasya niveśane bhṛśam utpatitaṃ ghoraṃ kuntī śuśrāva bhārata
english: Then Kuntī heard a great and terrible sound of anguish rising loudly from within the brahmin's dwelling, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: rorūyamāṇāṃs tān sarvān paridevayataś ca sā kāruṇyāt sādhubhāvāc ca devī rājan na cakṣame
english: Hearing all of them weeping and lamenting, the queen, O king, could not bear it out of compassion and her naturally noble disposition.

sanskrit: mathyamāneva duḥkhena hṛdayena pṛthā tataḥ uvāca bhīmaṃ kalyāṇī kṛpānvitam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: With her heart churning as if with grief, the auspicious Pṛthā then spoke these words of compassion to Bhīma.

sanskrit: vasāmaḥ susukhaṃ putra brāhmaṇasya niveśane ajñātā dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ satkṛtā vītamanyavaḥ
english: "We are dwelling in great happiness, my son, in this brahmin's house — unknown to the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, honoured and free from anger.

sanskrit: sā cintaye sadā putra brāhmaṇasyāsya kiṃ nv aham priyaṃ kuryām iti gṛhe yat kuryur uṣitāḥ sukham
english: I always think, my son, 'What can I do that is dear to this brahmin?' — just as those who dwell as guests should do to bring happiness to the household.

sanskrit: etāvān puruṣas tāta kṛtaṃ yasmin na naśyati yāvac ca kuryād anyo 'sya kuryād abhyadhikaṃ tataḥ
english: A man is as great as the good deed he does that does not perish — and as long as another might do something for him, he should do something more than that.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsya duḥkham āpatitaṃ dhruvam tatrāsya yadi sāhāyyaṃ kuryāma sukṛtaṃ bhavet
english: Now some definite sorrow has fallen upon this brahmin — if we were to help him in it, that would be a meritorious deed."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca jñāyatām asya yad duḥkhaṃ yataś caiva samutthitam vidite vyavasiṣyāmi yady api syāt suduṣkaram
english: Bhīma said: "Let us find out what his sorrow is and from where it has arisen — once it is known, I shall resolve it, even if it should be exceedingly difficult."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā hi kathayantau tau bhūyaḥ śuśruvatuḥ svanam ārtijaṃ tasya viprasya sabhāryasya viśāṃ pate
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the two of them were speaking thus, they again heard the sound of anguish from that brahmin along with his wife, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: antaḥpuraṃ tatas tasya brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ viveśa kuntī tvaritā baddhavatseva saurabhī
english: Kuntī then quickly entered the inner apartments of that noble brahmin, like a cow hastening toward her tethered calf.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tatra bhāryayā ca sutena ca duhitrā caiva sahitaṃ dadarśa vikṛtānanam
english: She then saw that brahmin there with his wife, his son, and his daughter — all of them with distorted faces.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca dhig idaṃ jīvitaṃ loke 'nalasāram anarthakam duḥkhamūlaṃ parādhīnaṃ bhṛśam apriyabhāgi ca
english: The brahmin said: "Fie upon this life in the world — it is insubstantial as fire, purposeless, rooted in sorrow, dependent on others, and greatly burdened with the unpleasant.

sanskrit: jīvite paramaṃ duḥkhaṃ jīvite paramo jvaraḥ jīvite vartamānasya dvandvānām āgamo dhruvaḥ
english: In living there is supreme sorrow; in living there is supreme fever; for one who lives in the world, the coming of life's opposites is inevitable.

sanskrit: ekātmāpi hi dharmārthau kāmaṃ ca na niṣevate etaiś ca viprayogo 'pi duḥkhaṃ paramakaṃ matam
english: Even a single person cannot fully pursue dharma, artha, and kama all at once; and separation from these too is considered the greatest sorrow.

sanskrit: āhuḥ ke cit paraṃ mokṣaṃ sa ca nāsti kathaṃ cana arthaprāptau ca narakaḥ kṛtsna evopapadyate
english: Some declare liberation to be the highest good, but that can never be attained; and in the acquisition of wealth, the whole of hell is incurred.

sanskrit: arthepsutā paraṃ duḥkhaṃ arthaprāptau tato 'dhikam jātasnehasya cārtheṣu viprayoge mahattaram
english: In desiring wealth there is supreme sorrow; in the actual gaining of wealth there is even more; and for one who has grown attached to riches, separation from them is the greatest sorrow of all.
